quotes.topic: Preferred finger pairs for adjacent strings
quotes.verbatim_quote: The main ways to pluck adjacent strings is with the p and i fingers, or i and m fingers.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the canonical two-finger combinations for multi-string plucking.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Regardless of which fingers you use, ensure that both fingers sound the notes simultaneously.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Core synchronization rule separating clean ensemble fingerstyle from ragged arpeggiation.

quotes.verbatim_quote: Now you need to negotiate a string skip in the plucking hand, hence the use of pm and ia as marked.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Introduces the string-skip fingering rule specific to 6th intervals.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Ensure that your wrist is rolled slightly more towards the headstock to allow more space between the
index finger and thumb.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Foundational hand-position rule preventing mechanical failure when plucking adjacent strings.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
3 notes at once, it’s preferable to use pi m, or i ma, so it’s worth practicing both these
combinations.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Specifies preferred finger groupings for three-voice chords.

quotes.topic: Little finger usage and four-finger maximum
quotes.verbatim_quote:
I rarely use the little finger (c) on the right hand with fingerstyle technique — I tend to stick to 4-note
voicings as a maximum
quotes.why_load_bearing: Establishes a practical voicing ceiling and justifies omitting the weak little finger.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Using a mirror to see what your hand is doing when you’re developing techniques like these is very
useful to check you're doing things correctly.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Gives a concrete self-monitoring tool for catching hand-position errors.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
Notice that the thumb plays a note twice in a row. It’s quite natural for the thumb to do a double
pluck in these situations as it simplifies the picking fingering greatly.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Legitimizes and explains the thumb double-pluck as a deliberate simplifying strategy.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
If you find these exercises a challenge, it would be worth revising the general tips on hand position
and finger motion covered in the first lesson of this module.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Reinforces relaxation as the corrective principle when coordination breaks down.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
thumb independence in a picking pattern context —- the thumb moves
between the 5th and 4th strings as you play the exercise.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Identifies thumb string-switching as a distinct skill targeted by the exercise.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
I would suggest practicing the picking pattern over a single chord for a while until you get it under
your fingers first. After that, start to build the pattern over the full chord progression.

For most of these exercises, I suggest you try another plucking finger combination on the repeats to
help work out more picking combinations.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Mandates alternate fingerings on repeats to expand picking vocabulary.
